physicalNotes: Radius 0.232849 Jupiter radii from Newton et al. 2022 (2022AJ....164..115N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..115N/abstract): 16,646.8 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.023 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 13.7905315 d
sources.shape: Newton et al. 2022 (2022AJ....164..115N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname NEWTON_ET_AL__2022): a/R* 32.9; Newton et al. 2022 (2022AJ....164..115N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname NEWTON_ET_AL__2022): inclination 89.41 degrees

sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2459704.448013 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 14 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
